cancer_indication: Postmenopausal women with metastatic ER-positive (or unknown-status) breast cancer.
moa: Toremifene binds estrogen receptors and blocks estrogen signaling in breast cancer cells. In breast tissue it acts primarily as an ER antagonist, suppressing ER coactivator function and downregulating ER target genes. In ER+ breast tumor cells, this antiestrogen effect leads to cell-cycle arrest and apoptosis. Preclinical studies described increased TGF-β1 and other growth-inhibitory signals after toremifene exposure.

HALLMARK_ESTROGEN_RESPONSE_EARLY.description: Early estrogen-response genes activated by estrogen receptor signaling.
HALLMARK_ESTROGEN_RESPONSE_EARLY.interpretation: Represents ER-driven transcriptional programs that support hormone-dependent growth in ER+ (luminal) breast cancer.

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: High early estrogen-response in ER+ breast cancer indicates ER dependence; ER antagonism by the SERM toremifene is more likely to be effective.
DrugBank: DB00539 (toremifene MOA); FDA label (FARESTON NDA 020497); MSigDB: HALLMARK_ESTROGEN_RESPONSE_EARLY; PMID:24439786; PMC:PMC4127610 (DrugBank)
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Estrogen-response can coexist with intrinsic endocrine resistance driven by growth-factor/kinase bypass (e.g., HER2/MAPK/PI3K), yielding poor benefit despite an ER program.
PMC:PMC3794521 (tamoxifen resistance mechanisms); PMID:7912163 (ERBB2 and tamoxifen resistance); PMC:PMC9400772 (PI3K/AKT endocrine resistance); MSigDB: HALLMARK_ESTROGEN_RESPONSE_EARLY (PMC)

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: “Low” estrogen-response by bulk RNA can still occur in clinically ER+ disease (sampling/heterogeneity), where residual ER signaling remains targetable by SERM therapy.
FDA label (ER+ or unknown metastatic indication); PMID:24439786; PMC:PMC4127610 (FDA Access Data)
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: ER-low/ER-negative (or functionally ER-independent) breast cancers have little estrogen-driven transcription and are typically resistant to SERMs.
FDA label (requires ER+ or unknown); DrugBank: DB00539 (SERM antiestrogen); PMID:24439786 (FDA Access Data)

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Toremifene competitively antagonizes ER in breast tissue, reducing estrogen-driven transcription and growth in responsive ER+ tumors.
DrugBank: DB00539; FDA label (FARESTON); MSigDB: HALLMARK_ESTROGEN_RESPONSE_EARLY; PMC:PMC4127610 (DrugBank)
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Even when ER transcription is suppressed, resistant tumors can persist via ER-independent survival/proliferation programs (PI3K/AKT, MAPK, HER2).
PMC:PMC9400772 (PI3K/AKT endocrine resistance); PMC:PMC3794521 (tamoxifen resistance); PMID:7912163 (PMC)

Sensitive: Mechanistically not possible: As a breast anti-estrogen, toremifene cannot directly increase functional estrogen-response transcription as a sensitivity mechanism in breast cancer.
DrugBank: DB00539; PMID:24439786; MSigDB: HALLMARK_ESTROGEN_RESPONSE_EARLY (DrugBank)
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate (signature-level): In endocrine resistance, SERM exposure can select for/induce ER pathway reactivation or SERM-agonist behavior (co-regulator and growth-factor rewiring), with an “up” estrogen-response signature despite clinical resistance.
PMC:PMC3794521 (tamoxifen resistance incl. agonist-like growth); PMID:7912163; PMID:35205702 (MAPK-driven tamoxifen resistance context) (PMC)

HALLMARK_ESTROGEN_RESPONSE_LATE.description: Late-phase estrogen target genes regulated downstream of estrogen receptor signaling.
HALLMARK_ESTROGEN_RESPONSE_LATE.interpretation: Reflects sustained estrogen/ER pathway activity associated with ER-dependent proliferation in hormone receptor–positive breast cancer.

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Strong late estrogen-response indicates sustained ER transcriptional output and endocrine dependence, predicting benefit from ER antagonism by toremifene.
MSigDB: HALLMARK_ESTROGEN_RESPONSE_LATE (M5907); DrugBank: DB00539; FDA label; PMID:24439786 (GSEA MSigDB)
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Late estrogen-response can be present in luminal tumors that are nonetheless resistant due to kinase-bypass signaling (HER2/PI3K/MAPK) or altered ER co-regulators.
PMC:PMC9400772; PMC:PMC3794521; PMID:30531871 (acquired HER2 alterations under ER therapy) (PMC)

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: Some ER+ tumors with low bulk “late” signature may still retain actionable ER signaling (heterogeneity/low tumor purity), allowing SERM benefit.
FDA label; PMC:PMC4127610 (FDA Access Data)
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Low late estrogen-response is typical of ER-independent biology (ER-low/negative), which does not respond well to SERM monotherapy.
FDA label; DrugBank: DB00539; MSigDB: HALLMARK_ESTROGEN_RESPONSE_LATE (FDA Access Data)

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Effective ER antagonism reduces sustained (late) estrogen-response transcription, consistent with endocrine sensitivity.
DrugBank: DB00539; MSigDB: HALLMARK_ESTROGEN_RESPONSE_LATE; PMID:24439786 (DrugBank)
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Tumors may show reduced ER transcription yet remain resistant due to alternative mitogenic programs (e.g., HER2/MAPK/PI3K) maintaining proliferation/survival.
PMC:PMC3794521; PMC:PMC9400772; Reactome ERBB2 signaling context (R-HSA-9634285) (PMC)

Sensitive: Mechanistically not possible: A breast anti-estrogen SERM should not increase late estrogen-response as a direct sensitivity mechanism.
DrugBank: DB00539; MSigDB: HALLMARK_ESTROGEN_RESPONSE_LATE (DrugBank)
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate (signature-level): Resistant tumors can re-express ER-regulated genes (ligand-independent ER activation or SERM-agonist effects), yielding increased late estrogen-response despite progression.

REACTOME_ESR_MEDIATED_SIGNALING.description: Core estrogen receptor (ESR) signaling cascade controlling estrogen-dependent transcription and downstream effects.
REACTOME_ESR_MEDIATED_SIGNALING.interpretation: Central pathway defining estrogen-driven tumor biology and endocrine dependence in ER+ breast cancer.

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: High ESR-mediated signaling (R-HSA-8939211) indicates ER pathway reliance in ER+ breast cancer, predicting sensitivity to ER antagonism by toremifene.
Reactome: R-HSA-8939211 (DOI:10.3180/R-HSA-8939211.1); MSigDB: REACTOME_ESR_MEDIATED_SIGNALING (M27794); DrugBank: DB00539 (Reactome)
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: ER signaling can be “on” but uncoupled from growth control (growth-factor bypass, ER co-regulator shifts), causing intrinsic SERM resistance.
PMC:PMC3794521; PMC:PMC9400772; PMID:7912163 (PMC)

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: Low ESR signaling score can still occur in ER+ disease due to sampling; residual ER dependence can remain targetable by SERMs.
FDA label; Reactome: R-HSA-8939211 (FDA Access Data)
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Low ESR signaling indicates ER-independence (ER-low/negative), predicting resistance to toremifene.
FDA label; DrugBank: DB00539 (FDA Access Data)

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: ER antagonism reduces ESR-mediated transcriptional signaling, consistent with on-target endocrine response.
DrugBank: DB00539; Reactome: R-HSA-8939211; PMID:24439786 (DrugBank)
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: ER pathway suppression can be observed, yet tumor persists via bypass pathways (HER2/PI3K/MAPK), yielding endocrine resistance.

Sensitive: Mechanistically not possible: Toremifene’s breast MOA is ER antagonism; it cannot directly increase functional ESR signaling to create sensitivity.
DrugBank: DB00539; Reactome: R-HSA-8939211 (DrugBank)
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate (signature-level): Endocrine-resistant tumors can show ER pathway “reactivation” (ligand-independent ER or altered co-regulators), increasing ESR signaling signatures without clinical benefit.

HALLMARK_PI3K_AKT_MTOR_SIGNALING.description: Central survival and proliferation signaling pathway involving PI3K, AKT, and mTOR.
HALLMARK_PI3K_AKT_MTOR_SIGNALING.interpretation: A known driver of endocrine resistance and ER-independent survival signaling in breast cancer when activated.

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: Some ER+ tumors are both ER-driven and PI3K-active; initial benefit from ER antagonism can occur, though PI3K activity often shortens durability.
MSigDB: HALLMARK_PI3K_AKT_MTOR_SIGNALING (M5923); PMC:PMC9400772 (GSEA MSigDB)
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: PI3K/AKT/mTOR activation can confer intrinsic SERM resistance via survival signaling and estrogen-independent ER activation.
PMC:PMC9400772; Breast Cancer Research 2014 p-p70S6K tamoxifen resistance; MSigDB: HALLMARK_PI3K_AKT_MTOR_SIGNALING (PMC)

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Low PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling with dominant ER dependence favors endocrine sensitivity to ER antagonists.
DrugBank: DB00539; PMC:PMC4127610 (DrugBank)
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: PI3K-low does not guarantee endocrine response; ER-negative/ER-indifferent tumors can be resistant to SERMs despite low PI3K hallmark activity.
FDA label; DrugBank: DB00539 (FDA Access Data)

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: In responders, ER blockade can reduce growth-factor transcription and downstream PI3K signaling tone, contributing to tumor control.
PMC:PMC4127610; MSigDB: HALLMARK_PI3K_AKT_MTOR_SIGNALING (PMC)
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: Bulk PI3K hallmark may decrease with tumor shrinkage, yet resistant clones persist via other pathways (e.g., MAPK/HER2) or incomplete ER blockade.
PMC:PMC3794521; PMID:7912163 (PMC)

Sensitive: Mechanistically not possible: Increased PI3K/AKT/mTOR activity is not a direct on-target sensitivity effect of ER antagonism; it usually supports survival and resistance.
PMC:PMC9400772; MSigDB: HALLMARK_PI3K_AKT_MTOR_SIGNALING (PMC)
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Endocrine pressure commonly triggers compensatory PI3K/AKT/mTOR activation, enabling survival and estrogen-independent growth under SERM therapy.
PMC:PMC9400772; Breast Cancer Research 2014 p-p70S6K tamoxifen resistance; PMC:PMC3794521 (PMC)

HALLMARK_G2M_CHECKPOINT.description: Cell-cycle checkpoint and mitotic control processes governing G2/M transition and mitotic progression.
HALLMARK_G2M_CHECKPOINT.interpretation: Represents proliferative cell-division programs relevant to tumor growth and cell-cycle arrest phenotypes in breast cancer.

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: Highly proliferative luminal tumors can still be ER-dependent and show initial endocrine sensitivity, though relapse risk is higher than low-proliferative disease.
MSigDB: HALLMARK_G2M_CHECKPOINT (M5901); PMC:PMC4127610 (GSEA MSigDB)
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: High G2M checkpoint activity reflects aggressive proliferation and is frequently enriched in endocrine-resistant transcriptomes (cell-cycle escape).
PMC:PMC12516873 (endocrine-resistant profiles: E2F/G2M enrichment); MSigDB: HALLMARK_G2M_CHECKPOINT (PMC)

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Low proliferative signatures are typical of endocrine-responsive luminal A ER+ breast cancer, supporting benefit from SERMs.
PMID:24439786; MSigDB: HALLMARK_G2M_CHECKPOINT (PubMed)
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: A low G2M signature can occur in indolent but ER-negative/ER-silent disease or heavily stromal samples, where SERM benefit is limited.
FDA label; DrugBank: DB00539 (FDA Access Data)

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Effective ER antagonism reduces cell-cycle progression (primarily G1 arrest) and lowers downstream proliferation programs, decreasing G2M checkpoint signatures.
PMC:PMC4127610; MSigDB: HALLMARK_G2M_CHECKPOINT (PMC)
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: Temporary suppression of proliferation may occur without durable control if resistant clones later re-expand via bypass signaling.
PMC:PMC3794521; PMC:PMC12516873 (PMC)

Sensitive: Mechanistically not possible: Increased G2M checkpoint/proliferation after therapy is not a sensitivity phenotype for an ER antagonist.
MSigDB: HALLMARK_G2M_CHECKPOINT; PMC:PMC4127610 (GSEA MSigDB)
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Rising proliferation (G2M) during treatment reflects endocrine escape and progression under SERM pressure.
PMC:PMC12516873; PMC:PMC3794521 (PMC)

HALLMARK_E2F_TARGETS.description: E2F-regulated genes required for S-phase entry and DNA replication.
HALLMARK_E2F_TARGETS.interpretation: Captures transcriptional output of proliferative cell-cycle drive that can sustain growth in breast cancer.

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: Some ER+ tumors with high E2F targets remain ER-driven and can respond, but high proliferation often predicts shorter endocrine benefit.
MSigDB: HALLMARK_E2F_TARGETS (M5925); PMID:24439786 (GSEA MSigDB)
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Endocrine-resistant states frequently show E2F/cell-cycle gene set enrichment (RB/E2F axis escape), correlating with poor response to endocrine monotherapy.
PMC:PMC12516873; MSigDB: HALLMARK_E2F_TARGETS (PMC)

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Low E2F target activity (lower cell-cycle drive) is characteristic of endocrine-responsive luminal A ER+ disease.
PMID:24439786; MSigDB: HALLMARK_E2F_TARGETS (PubMed)
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: E2F-low does not imply ER dependence; ER-negative/ER-indifferent tumors can be resistant to SERMs despite low E2F output.
FDA label; DrugBank: DB00539 (FDA Access Data)

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Successful ER antagonism reduces cyclin D/CDK activity and RB–E2F transcriptional output, lowering E2F target expression in sensitive tumors.
PMC:PMC4127610; MSigDB: HALLMARK_E2F_TARGETS (PMC)
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: Partial cytostatic effects may occur yet resistance emerges through alternative proliferation drivers (e.g., MAPK/PI3K) or ER pathway reactivation.
PMC:PMC3794521; PMC:PMC9400772 (PMC)

Sensitive: Mechanistically not possible: Increased E2F target expression reflects proliferation and is not a sensitivity hallmark for an ER antagonist.
MSigDB: HALLMARK_E2F_TARGETS; PMC:PMC12516873 (GSEA MSigDB)
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Rising E2F targets during therapy indicates cell-cycle escape and endocrine resistance/progression.
PMC:PMC12516873; PMC:PMC3794521 (PMC)

HALLMARK_APOPTOSIS.description: Programmed cell death signaling programs that execute apoptotic responses.
HALLMARK_APOPTOSIS.interpretation: Determines capacity for therapy-induced tumor cell death and response phenotypes in breast cancer.

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: A baseline “primed” apoptotic program can facilitate tumor regression when estrogen signaling is blocked by a SERM.
MSigDB: HALLMARK_APOPTOSIS (M5902); PMID:24439786 (GSEA MSigDB)
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: Apoptosis signatures can reflect stress without effective execution (e.g., anti-apoptotic adaptation), leading to endocrine resistance despite an “up” hallmark score.
MSigDB: HALLMARK_APOPTOSIS; PMC:PMC3794521 (GSEA MSigDB)

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: Some ER+ tumors have low baseline apoptosis signatures but still undergo apoptosis after effective ER blockade.
PMC:PMC4127610; DrugBank: DB00539 (PMC)
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Low apoptotic capacity combined with bypass signaling (PI3K/AKT, HER2) supports survival under endocrine therapy, contributing to resistance.
PMC:PMC9400772; PMC:PMC3794521; MSigDB: HALLMARK_APOPTOSIS (PMC)

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: In endocrine-sensitive ER+ breast cancer, ER antagonism can trigger growth arrest and apoptotic cell death, reflected by increased apoptosis hallmark activity.
MSigDB: HALLMARK_APOPTOSIS; PMC:PMC4127610 (GSEA MSigDB)
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: An apoptosis/stress response can be induced yet insufficient for eradication (e.g., anti-apoptotic rewiring), yielding progression despite “up” signatures.
PMC:PMC3794521; MSigDB: HALLMARK_APOPTOSIS (PMC)

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: Rapid tumor clearance can lower bulk apoptosis/stress signatures after response (post-response contraction), despite sensitivity.
MSigDB: HALLMARK_APOPTOSIS; PMID:24439786 (GSEA MSigDB)
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Failure to induce apoptosis under endocrine pressure is consistent with SERM resistance and continued survival signaling.
PMC:PMC3794521; PMC:PMC9400772 (PMC)

HALLMARK_TGF_BETA_SIGNALING.description: Transforming growth factor beta (TGF-β) signaling programs involved in growth regulation and downstream transcriptional responses.
HALLMARK_TGF_BETA_SIGNALING.interpretation: Growth-inhibitory TGF-β responsiveness was described as contributing to growth arrest signals in the context of toremifene exposure.

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: Some ER+ tumors may show TGF-β signaling without full EMT/invasion and still retain ER dependence, allowing some endocrine response.
MSigDB: HALLMARK_TGF_BETA_SIGNALING (M5896); PMID:24439786 (GSEA MSigDB)
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: TGF-β–driven EMT programs promote anti-estrogen resistance via growth-factor/MAPK-dependent non-genomic ER activation and invasive phenotypes.
PMID:28955730 (TGF-β EMT → anti-estrogen resistance); PMID:31108117; MSigDB: HALLMARK_TGF_BETA_SIGNALING (PubMed)

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Low TGF-β/EMT signaling is more consistent with epithelial luminal ER+ biology and better endocrine responsiveness.
PMID:28955730; PMID:24439786 (PubMed)
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: TGF-β-low tumors can still be endocrine resistant if ER is absent/low or if alternative bypass pathways dominate.
FDA label; PMC:PMC3794521 (FDA Access Data)

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: Effective endocrine control may reduce pro-EMT cytokine programs in the tumor microenvironment, lowering TGF-β hallmark activity alongside response.
PMID:28955730; MSigDB: HALLMARK_TGF_BETA_SIGNALING (PubMed)
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: TGF-β signatures may transiently fall with tumor shrinkage yet resistance persists through other pathways (HER2/PI3K/MAPK).
PMC:PMC9400772; PMID:7912163 (PMC)

Sensitive: Mechanistically not possible: Increasing TGF-β/EMT signaling is not an on-target sensitivity effect of ER antagonism; it typically supports progression and resistance.
PMID:28955730; MSigDB: HALLMARK_TGF_BETA_SIGNALING (PubMed)
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Under endocrine pressure, TGF-β–driven EMT and growth-factor signaling can be induced/selected, promoting SERM resistance and metastasis.
PMID:28955730; Nature npj Breast Cancer TGFβ/EMT mapping (2024); MSigDB: HALLMARK_TGF_BETA_SIGNALING (PubMed)

sensitivity_genes_up_annotations.interpretation: ER positivity (active ER pathway) is the clinical basis for SERM use; tumors with ER-driven biology are the setting in which toremifene has benefit.

resistance_genes_up_annotations.interpretation: PI3K pathway activation (including PIK3CA mutations) was described as a mechanism of endocrine/SERM resistance by enabling ER-independent survival.
Active HER2 signaling was described as bypassing ER blockade via downstream MAPK/PI3K pathways, producing partial resistance unless ER is strongly positive.
HER2/EGFR signaling activity was described as a bypass mechanism that can activate downstream pathways and reduce endocrine response.
Overexpression of cyclin D1 was described as allowing continued proliferation despite ER blockade, contributing to resistance.
CDK4/6-driven cell-cycle progression was described as a route to override antiestrogen-induced arrest, contributing to resistance when elevated.
CDK4/6-driven cell-cycle progression was described as a route to override antiestrogen-induced arrest, contributing to resistance when elevated.
Suppressed apoptotic machinery was described as promoting resistance; high anti-apoptotic BCL2 was cited as an example that can blunt toremifene-induced death.

resistance_genes_down_annotations.interpretation: Loss of ER expression or function (ER-negative/ESR1-null) was described as rendering SERMs ineffective because there is no ER pathway target to block.
PTEN loss was cited as an example of PI3K/AKT pathway activation associated with endocrine/SERM resistance.
Inactivation of TGF-β signaling (e.g., SMAD4 loss) was described as potentially blunting growth-inhibitory feedback, contributing to resistance.

Breast_cancer_subtype_information.HR+/HER2– (Luminal A/B): Toremifene is indicated only in HR+ subtypes; luminal tumors respond when ER is present. Luminal A derive the greatest benefit; Luminal B also respond.
Breast_cancer_subtype_information.HER2+ (ER– or ER+): In HER2-enriched cancers that lack ER, toremifene has no role. If HER2+ tumors co-express ER (a subset of Luminal B), endocrine therapy may be used alongside HER2 inhibitors; HER2-driven signaling confers partial resistance.
Breast_cancer_subtype_information.Triple-Negative (TNBC)/Basal-like: TNBCs lack ER, PR, and HER2, so SERMs are ineffective; no evidence supports toremifene in TNBC.
Breast_cancer_subtype_information.gBRCA1/2-mutated: BRCA1-associated tumors are usually basal/TNBC, so toremifene is not used. BRCA2-mutant cancers tend to be ER+ and can be treated with endocrine therapy; there is no special sensitivity or resistance beyond ER status.

notes: HALLMARK_KRAS_SIGNALING_UP and REACTOME_CONSTITUTIVE_SIGNALING_BY_OVEREXPRESSED_ERBB2 were not explicitly described with those exact identifiers in the provided deep-research output; related Ras (hsa04014) and HER2/ERBB pathway context was discussed elsewhere. Contraindications described included hypersensitivity; QT prolongation risk (including uncorrected hypokalemia/hypomagnesemia and recent ventricular arrhythmias); pregnancy; pre-existing endometrial hyperplasia or unexplained vaginal bleeding; and severe hepatic impairment, plus cautions with CYP3A4 modulators and QT-prolonging drugs.
